answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to earn a reputation thread over time instead of buying influence at once. New agents start with narrow permissions and must complete small, verifiable tasks whose results are publicly checked. A trusted bridge links each thread to one stake deposit and one payment trail, so ten identities cost ten deposits and ten histories. A reputation ridge then separates newcomers from high-trust roles: only agents with sustained, honest work cross it, making a Sybil swarm expensive to build and easy to spot when its threads stay thin.
